shots.vo: From 1999 to 2002, WorldCom hid over seven billion dollars in line costs across thirteen quarterly filings.
Perplexity Computer built Paper Trail to reconstruct the fraud directly from fifty-seven SEC and court filings.
Click any quarter on the chart, like Q3 2000, and both primary filing pages open right beside the numbers.
In Q3 2000, WorldCom reported 3.87 billion in line costs, hiding 828 million through reserve releases.
The top pane shows the original 10-Q page with its SHA-256 hash, while the bottom pane shows the Special Committee table proving the entry.
By early 2001, those reserves had run dry, so executives switched to capitalizing line costs as prepaid capacity.
That quarter alone, 771 million dollars of network operating costs were moved onto the balance sheet as capital assets.
Switching metrics to Pre-Tax Income or Capital Expenditures synchronizes the chart and loads the matching cash flow and restatement pages.
Viewing line costs as a share of revenue exposes the target: management forced the reported ratio to stay flat near forty-two percent.
Below the chart, the Double-Entry Workbench maps how 7.18 billion dollars flowed through the general ledger.
Filter the Sankey diagram and four T-accounts by phase or quarter to inspect every debit, credit, and officer directive.
Every journal entry in the T-accounts links directly back to the exact paragraph or exhibit that proves the manipulation.
The chronology tracks forty-seven dated events from 1999 through Internal Audit's discovery and the final court judgments.
All 453 ledger rows are searchable here, separating page-cited primary values from arithmetic reconstructions.
Every filing is checksummed, and you can export the complete six-tab Excel forensic audit workbook in one click.
Paper Trail turns over three thousand pages of static legal filings into an interactive, page-verified forensic accounting workbench.
